label: agent-mesh-built
context:
AGENT MESH — Multi-agent coordination layer for Hermes. Built and tested. Files:

1. ~/.hermes/plugins/evey-mesh/mesh_db.py — Shared SQLite DB with WAL mode. Tables: presence, activity_stream, file_locks, task_board, messages. All tested.

2. ~/.hermes/plugins/evey-mesh/__init__.py — Plugin providing 4 tools: mesh_status, mesh_message, mesh_task, mesh_lock. Hooks: agent:start, agent:step, agent:end.

3. ~/.hermes/plugins/evey-mesh/plugin.yaml — Plugin manifest.

4. ~/.hermes/hooks/agent-mesh/HOOK.yaml + handler.py — Hook handler that registers presence, heartbeats, logs tool calls, deregisters on end.

5. ~/hermes-agent/gateway/run.py (line 2299-2322) — Mesh context injection. When other agents are active, injects their activity, locks, messages, and tasks into the session context.

Tested features:
- Two agents see each other's presence
- File lock conflict detection (Agent 2 denied when Agent 1 holds lock)
- Cross-agent messaging with read tracking
- Shared task board with create/claim/complete
- Activity stream showing other agents' tool calls
- Auto-expiring locks (TTL-based)

GATEWAY RESTART NEEDED to activate all of this.
active_tasks: Agent Mesh plugin built — needs gateway restart to activate
decisions: SQLite with WAL mode for coordination — no external broker needed, local-only, zero dependencies
Mesh context only injected when other agents are detected — solo agents see nothing
File locks are TTL-based with auto-expiry — prevents deadlocks from crashed agents
Hook handler uses lazy-load to avoid import errors on gateway startup
next_steps: Restart gateway with safe-restart.sh to activate mesh. Then open two hermes sessions and test live coordination.
